title: Promise.all, allSettled, race, any
learningObjectives: Explain promise.all, allsettled, race, any and implement reliable browser event and network workflows.

understand.concept: Promise.all fulfils when all inputs fulfil and rejects on the first rejection. allSettled waits for every input and reports each outcome. race settles with the first settled input. any fulfils with the first fulfilled input and rejects with AggregateError if all reject.
understand.whyItMatters: The combinator should match the coordination policy required by the feature: all results, all outcomes, first result, or first success.
understand.analogy: These methods represent different group decision rules for a set of asynchronous jobs.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript scheduling, HTTP semantics, and browser security follow platform standards.

explain.narrative: allSettled waits for every promise and returns a status record for each one.

examples.explanation: allSettled waits for every promise and returns a status record for each one.
examples.expectedOutput: Console or UI output demonstrates the concept; network examples require a configured endpoint.

practise.guidedTask: Run the same inputs through all four combinators and handle each rejection case.
practise.independentTask: Build an asynchronous feature with explicit states, cancellation, and error handling. Document which failures are safe to retry.
hints: Separate HTTP errors from network and parsing errors.
Use bounded retries only for suitable operations.
Tie UI updates to the latest active request.

questions.prompt: Which method waits for all inputs to settle and reports each outcome?
questions.explanation: allSettled returns an outcome record for every input after all have settled.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable approach to network-driven UI?
options: Model loading, empty, success, failure, and cancellation states
Assume every fulfilled fetch means HTTP success
questions.answer: Model loading, empty, success, failure, and cancellation states
questions.explanation: Explicit states and bounded recovery make network interfaces predictable and safe.
